_comment: Structural parameters, single source of truth. tools/gen-params.py
§9 calls this a MECHANISM decision rather than a convention, and is
specific about why: ROB depth exists as a swept knob in the timing model
(Stage 4b) and as an RTL parameter, nothing otherwise prevents them from
drifting, and drift means a correlation run silently comparing two
differently-sized machines -- a failure that looks like a timing bug.
WHAT IS DECIDED HERE: nothing about sizing. §1 asks for everything to be
structurally parameterized as config knobs so that design-space
exploration happens before any of it becomes area/timing commitment, and
§2 puts the sizing decisions at Stage 4a with the exploration at 4b. The
values below are placeholders that make the mechanism exercisable.
The `status` field is the point of this file as much as the values are.
`isa` means it follows from the locked ISA and is not ours to sweep;
`provisional` means a placeholder awaiting the stage named in `decided_at`.
Mixing the two silently is how a sweep ends up varying something the

params.name: CCV_WARP_LANES
params.doc: Lanes per warp. A logical GPR holds 32 lanes, one element each, at every chwidth.

params.name: CCV_GPRS
params.source: ISA v1.6 §1, O-25 -- settled, and not by the spill data
params.doc: Logical GPRs. Widening to 32 is a reset of the encoding, not a parameter change: Format J overruns 16 bits and Format A-double-prime falls to a 1-bit opcode.

params.name: CCV_PREDS
params.source: ISA v1.6 §1 -- provisional pending compiler data; measured pressure is 1-2 of 4
params.doc: Logical predicates. A performance parameter, not a structural ceiling, since O-19 made the file spillable.

params.name: CCV_BARRIER_ENTRIES
params.source: ISA v1.6 §3, Format E -- 6-bit barrier ID
params.doc: Barrier table entries. The table is a §7 formal target.

params.name: CCV_DATAPATH_BITS
params.doc: Physical datapath width. Kept full by coalescing independent 32-lane instructions, never by widening one.

params.name: CCV_IQ_ENTRIES
params.doc: PLACEHOLDER. Issue queue entries. §2 flags this as directly constrained by the wakeup/select timing budget: at 25 NGD the entry count and the simultaneous result-bus broadcast width are what must fit one pass.

params.name: CCV_PRF_ROWS
params.doc: PLACEHOLDER. Physical register file rows, each CCV_DATAPATH_BITS wide. Sub-row slices are the buddy/slab allocator's business (backend-context.md §5.4), not a separate parameter.

params.name: CCV_TIER1_WARPS
params.doc: PLACEHOLDER. Resident warps in the active SMT tier.

params.name: CCV_TIER2_WARPS
params.doc: PLACEHOLDER. Resident warps in the backing SMT tier.

params.name: CCV_NGD_BUDGET
params.source: §2 -- ~1.5 GHz at Vmin 0.55 V on an N3E-class process
params.doc: Normalized gate delay available in one cycle. Per-block budgets are recorded against this at Stage 2 and 4a. OPEN (§2): whether 25 is the Vmin-corner number or a nominal one -- at 0.55 V variation and the wire/gate delay ratio both worsen, so headroom at nominal does not translate linearly.
